hero.headline: U.S. and Iran reach tentative agreement to extend ceasefire, awaiting Trump approval
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have moved closer to extending their two-week ceasefire beyond its April 22 expiration date, with Pakistani officials actively mediating negotiations between the two sides.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said on Wednesday that while the U.S. had not "formally" requested an extension, Washington remained "very much engaged in these negotiations." She indicated the White House feels "good about the prospects of a deal," though she cautioned that "nothing is official until you hear it from us here at the White House."

Pakistan's military leadership is playing a central role in the diplomatic efforts. Field Marshal Asim Munir led a delegation to Tehran on Wednesday to convey messages from Washington while arranging a second round of ceasefire talks. The delegation included Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi. Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is also traveling to Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Turkey to coordinate support for peace efforts among regional powers.

Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said both sides have continued exchanging messages even after 21 hours of talks in Islamabad ended without agreement over the weekend. "During this visit, the views of both sides are likely to be discussed in detail," Baghaei said.

However, significant obstacles remain. Sources in Tehran indicated Iran has demanded an end to Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a precondition for continuing negotiations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested Wednesday that his country has not committed to any ceasefire. He stated that Israeli forces would continue striking Hezbollah in Lebanon and that he had instructed the military to expand a security zone through ongoing operations.

The escalating tensions extend beyond Lebanon. The U.S. military implemented a naval blockade of Iranian ports after the Islamabad talks broke down, with American warships turning back nine vessels attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz, including a Chinese-owned tanker that has been sanctioned by the U.S.

Iran's military leadership responded to the blockade with warnings. Major General Ali Abdollahi, leader of Iran's joint military command, said the military could halt trade in the Gulf region if the U.S. did not lift its port blockade. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated the administration was prepared to escalate financial pressure through secondary sanctions against countries and companies purchasing Iranian oil or holding Iranian assets.

Despite these tensions, both sides appear reluctant to return to full-scale conflict. Trump predicted a swift resolution, telling ABC News correspondent Jonathan Karl that the war could end either before the ceasefire expires or after a deal is reached.

Leavitt said a second round of negotiations would "very likely" be held in Islamabad, indicating the diplomatic process continues even as military and economic pressure intensifies.

cards.headline: U.S. officials say framework emerging for Strait of Hormuz reopening
cards.teaser: American officials report progress toward an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though President Trump has not yet approved the framework.
cards.body:
U.S. officials say they are closing in on an arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping passage that has been disrupted during the Iran conflict. The emerging framework has not yet received approval from President Trump.

The potential arrangement could create conditions for extending the current ceasefire and enable more substantive negotiations between the United States and Iran. Vice President Vance said the two countries are very close to a deal but not there yet, according to separate reports.

cards.headline: Netanyahu directs military to expand control of Gaza to 70%
cards.teaser: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the military to increase its control of Gaza, potentially violating the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has directed the Israel Defense Forces to expand their control of Gaza to 70%, according to BBC News reports. This represents a significant expansion of Israel's military presence in the territory.

The directive appears to conflict with the ceasefire agreement that Israel and Hamas reached in October 2025, which set specific limits on Israeli military operations in Gaza.

cards.headline: Dell Secures $9.7 Billion Pentagon Contract
cards.teaser: Dell Technologies won a $9.7 billion contract from the Department of Defense, following Michael Dell's early outreach to the Trump administration.
cards.body:
The Pentagon awarded Dell Technologies a $9.7 billion contract to streamline software purchases for the Department of Defense. The contract was announced by the Department of War on May 27, 2026.

Michael Dell courted President Trump early in his administration, and the company has received favorable treatment since. Trump acquired stock in Dell and publicly praised the company. The defense contract stands to benefit Trump's investment portfolio, as the president holds financial interests in the company.

cards.headline: US Mortgage Rates Climb to 6.53%, Highest in Nine Months
cards.teaser: The average long-term mortgage rate in the United States rose to 6.53%, reaching its highest level since August and dampening refinancing activity.
cards.body:
The average long-term mortgage rate in the United States climbed to 6.53%, the highest level recorded in nine months. The increase has pushed rates to their peak since August of the previous year.

Mortgage refinance demand dropped 18% as rates reached the highest level since August. Some home buyers have given up hope that mortgage rates will fall in the near term. Housing markets are adapting to the higher rate environment rather than freezing, according to industry analysis.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Hit Record Highs on US-Iran Deal Hopes
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs as investors reacted to reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations.
cards.body:
US stock markets reached new records as major indexes including the S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed into positive territory. Dell contributed to gains with strong earnings results.

Market optimism was bolstered by reports of progress in US-Iran negotiations. According to US officials, a ceasefire extension framework has been agreed, though approval from Trump and Iran's leadership is still pending. Oil prices fell over 1% on the reports of a potential deal.

hero.headline: Russian drone hits apartment building in Romania, injuring two
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in the eastern Romanian city of Galați on Friday, injuring two people and sparking a fire, according to Romania's defense ministry.

The unmanned aircraft was part of a Russian overnight attack on Ukraine when it entered Romanian airspace and crashed onto the roof of the residential structure. Romanian authorities tracked the drone on radar as it crossed into their territory during the military operations against Ukraine.

The impact triggered a fire at the building. Two people sustained cuts requiring medical treatment, and several residents were evacuated from the complex as a precaution.

Romania's defense ministry characterized the incident as an "irresponsible escalation" by Moscow. The country is a NATO member that shares a border with Ukraine, making the drone strike a direct breach of its airspace during the broader conflict.

Under NATO's collective defense provisions, an attack on one member state is considered an attack on all members of the alliance. Romania joined the military alliance in 2004. In response to the incident, Romanian military forces scrambled F-16 fighter jets.

The drone strike represents a notable escalation in terms of the conflict's impact on neighboring countries. While debris and ordnance from the Russia-Ukraine war have previously crossed into adjacent territories, this marks a direct strike on a NATO member's civilian infrastructure during active Russian military operations.

The international community has expressed ongoing concern about the spillover effects from the conflict, particularly regarding civilian safety in countries bordering Ukraine. The incident highlights the risks posed to neighboring populations as Russian forces conduct sustained attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure near boundary areas.

Officials documented the damage to the civilian residential building and the circumstances surrounding the drone's entry into Romanian airspace. The exact nature of the drone and the full extent of structural damage to the apartment complex were not detailed in official statements.

This occurrence adds to mounting tensions in the region as the conflict continues to affect territories beyond Ukraine's borders. The involvement of a NATO member state, even through an apparent accident rather than a deliberate attack, raises questions about military operations in proximity to alliance boundaries and the safety measures in place to prevent such incidents.

Romanian authorities are investigating the full details of how the drone breached their airspace and the circumstances that led to its crash into the residential building.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a launch pad in Florida during a test.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket caught fire and exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night during an engine test. The incident was captured on video.

The New Glenn is Blue Origin's heavy-lift launch vehicle designed to carry payloads to orbit. The explosion occurred ahead of a satellite launch that had been scheduled for the following week.

cards.headline: Portugal sets new record for hottest May day as heatwave hits Europe
cards.teaser: Portugal broke its record for the hottest May day as a heatwave spreads across Europe, with red alerts issued in Italy.
cards.body:
Portugal recorded its hottest May day on record as a severe heatwave swept across Europe. Italy issued red alerts due to the extreme temperatures affecting the continent.

The heatwave created widespread disruptions across multiple countries. In France, students sat their exams in schools experiencing intense heat, while informal workers in Delhi continued working despite temperatures reaching 45°C and growing health risks.

cards.headline: Delhi workers face health risks as temperatures reach 45 degrees Celsius
cards.teaser: Informal workers in Delhi continue their jobs despite temperatures hitting 45 degrees Celsius and growing health dangers.
cards.body:
As temperatures in Delhi peak at 45 degrees Celsius, the city's informal workers are continuing to work despite mounting health risks. The extreme heat poses particular dangers for those working outdoors without climate-controlled environments.

For many of Delhi's poor, the need to earn income outweighs safety concerns related to the extreme weather. Informal workers lack the option to stay indoors during the hottest parts of the day, creating a situation where economic survival takes precedence over health protection.

cards.teaser: The U.S. opened a temporary medical facility in Kenya to treat Americans exposed to Ebola, despite legal challenges and criticism.
cards.body:
The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment facility in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than bringing them back to the United States. The White House confirmed the facility on Wednesday.

Some health experts have criticized the approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could undermine treatment efforts. Despite initial opposition, including a Kenyan High Court block, the facility proceeded with its planned opening.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during engine test at Florida launch pad
cards.teaser: A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a test at Cape Canaveral, days before a planned satellite launch.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida during an engine-firing test Thursday night. The incident occurred ahead of a satellite launch that had been scheduled for the following week.

Video footage captured the moment of the explosion on the pad.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer reverses statement on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Governor Gretchen Whitmer said she would not run for president in 2028, then walked back the comment hours later.
cards.body:
Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer initially said she would not run for president in 2028, then reversed that statement within hours. The shift was reported by major news outlets including AP News.

Whitmer's comments come as Democrats begin positioning themselves for the 2028 presidential race. Her name has been mentioned among potential Democratic contenders being considered for the next election cycle.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra leads California governor's race in new poll
cards.teaser: A new poll shows Xavier Becerra opening a lead in the California governor's race, with a tight contest for second place.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra has opened a lead in the race to become California's next governor, according to a new poll reported by the Los Angeles Times and Politico. The poll also found Paris Hilton and Tom Steyer in a tight contest for second place.

The primary election is approaching, with CalMatters and the Los Angeles Times both publishing voter guides for undecided voters. AP News reported that California Democrats have shown lukewarm enthusiasm for their choices in the crowded race to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.

cards.headline: 14-year-old Shrey Parikh wins Scripps National Spelling Bee
cards.teaser: The 101st Scripps National Spelling Bee was decided by a rapid-fire spell-off, the third time the format has determined the winner.
cards.body:
Shrey Parikh, 14, claimed victory at the Scripps National Spelling Bee in a dramatic tiebreaker against fellow competitor Ishaan Gupta. The California teen entered the competition as a favorite and delivered under pressure, dominating the lightning-round spell-off.

In the 90-second tiebreaker, Parikh spelled 32 words correctly, significantly outpacing Gupta's 25 correct spellings. This marked the 101st year of the national spelling competition and the third time the bee has been decided by the rapid-fire spell-off format, which was introduced in 2021.

cards.headline: Russian drone crashes into Romanian apartment building, injuring two
cards.teaser: A Russian drone struck a residential building in Romania, causing injuries and a fire.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Galați, eastern Romania, on Friday, injuring two people who sustained cuts requiring medical treatment. The impact sparked a fire on the building's roof, and several residents were evacuated.

Romanian authorities said the drone was part of a Russian overnight attack on Ukraine and was tracked by radar as it crossed into Romanian airspace. Romania's defence ministry condemned the incident as an "irresponsible escalation" by Moscow, and the military scrambled F-16 fighter jets in response.

hero.headline: Anthropic Reaches $965 Billion Valuation, Surpassing OpenAI
hero.body:
Anthropic announced a Series H funding round that values the artificial intelligence company at $965 billion, making it the most valuable AI startup and surpassing rival OpenAI. The company raised $65 billion in the funding round.

The valuation places Anthropic close to the $1 trillion mark, a milestone previously reached by only a handful of technology companies. The funding represents one of the largest venture capital raises in the AI sector.

Anthropic develops Claude, an AI assistant that competes with OpenAI's ChatGPT and other large language models. The company has positioned itself as focused on AI safety and responsible development practices.

The funding comes as investor interest in artificial intelligence companies has surged following breakthroughs in generative AI technology. Major technology companies and venture capital firms have poured billions of dollars into AI startups over the past two years.

OpenAI, which had previously held the position as the most valuable AI startup, released ChatGPT in late 2022, sparking widespread adoption of AI chatbots and assistants. The company has raised billions from Microsoft and other investors.

Anthropic was founded by former OpenAI executives who left to start their own company. The startup has attracted investment from major technology companies including Google, which has committed billions to the company.

The AI industry has seen rapid growth as companies race to develop more advanced models and deploy them across various applications, from customer service to software development. The sector has drawn comparisons to previous technology booms, with some analysts questioning whether current valuations reflect sustainable business models.

The $965 billion valuation values Anthropic higher than many established Fortune 500 companies. The company will use the new capital to expand its research capabilities, increase computing infrastructure, and develop new AI products.

cards.teaser: A Blue Origin rocket exploded into a fireball during an engine test at a Florida launchpad, marking another setback for the Jeff Bezos-owned space company.
cards.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida during an engine-firing test on Thursday night. The explosion sent a massive fireball across the facility as the company was preparing for a satellite launch scheduled for the following week.

Jeff Bezos, who founded Blue Origin, described it as a very rough day for the company. The incident marks another operational setback for the aerospace firm as it continues developing its launch capabilities in the competitive commercial space industry.

cards.teaser: Oil prices dropped more than 1% following reports of a potential ceasefire agreement between the United States and Iran that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
cards.body:
Oil prices fell over 1% on Thursday following reports of a potential ceasefire extension between the United States and Iran. The framework of the deal has been agreed upon, though it still requires approval from Donald Trump and Iran's leadership. US officials indicated the nations are "very close" to finalizing the agreement.

The potential deal has boosted market sentiment globally. Stock markets rose on optimism about the agreement, with the Dow Jones and S&P 500 posting gains. Oil prices pared some gains as markets absorbed the news of the possible breakthrough in negotiations.

cards.teaser: SpaceX reduced its initial public offering valuation target to at least $1.8 trillion as the company prepares to go public.
cards.body:
SpaceX lowered its target valuation for its initial public offering to at least $1.8 trillion. The reduced target comes as the company moves forward with plans to sell shares to public investors for the first time.

The SpaceX IPO has generated significant investor interest, with 78% of the $80 billion offering already committed before the public launch. Financial analysts have raised concerns about whether the IPO represents a bubble in space sector investments, with some noting that other space stocks have not joined the valuation surge seen around SpaceX

hero.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket explodes during Florida test
hero.body:
A New Glenn rocket belonging to Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin company exploded during a ground test at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Thursday night, dealing a significant blow to the company's efforts to compete with SpaceX in the commercial spaceflight industry.

The explosion occurred at 9 p.m. ET during a scheduled "hotfire" test, in which the rocket's engines are ignited while the vehicle remains on the launchpad. A massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launch pad, with the blast creating an orange sky visible as far south as Fort Pierce, 115 miles away. Shockwaves from the explosion were felt across Florida's space coast, causing homes to shake in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach. Residents in South Carolina, hundreds of miles to the north, reported seeing a glow in the sky.

Bezos acknowledged the setback on social media, stating that all employees were accounted for and safe. "It's too early to know the root cause but we're already working to find it," he wrote. "Very rough day, but we'll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It's worth it." Emergency officials confirmed there was no threat from fumes or other hazards, though flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the incident. Blue Origin described the event as "an anomaly."

The explosion threatens NASA's ambitious timeline for lunar exploration. Just one day before the test failure, NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a 20 billion dollar lunar base. The New Glenn rocket was intended to launch landers to the Moon for NASA's Artemis Program, including vehicles that will transport astronauts to the lunar surface.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in a statement that the agency would work with Blue Origin to investigate the explosion and assess the impact on near-term missions and the broader Artemis program. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," he wrote.

This explosion marks the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the rocket ended up in the wrong orbit during a flight, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the vehicle. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared New Glenn to return to flight the previous week.

Blue Origin and SpaceX are both competing for NASA contracts under the Artemis program, which aims to return humans to the Moon for the first time since 1972 and establish a sustainable lunar presence. Elon Musk responded to the explosion on social media, noting that "rockets are hard."

cards.headline: AWS and Cloudflare rebuild internet infrastructure for AI agents
cards.teaser: Major cloud providers are redesigning their infrastructure to handle machine-generated internet traffic as AI agents move into production.
cards.body:
Cloud infrastructure companies including AWS and Cloudflare are rebuilding parts of the internet to accommodate AI agents moving from experimental use to production deployment. The redesign focuses on handling traffic generated by machines rather than human users.

The shift reflects expectations that AI agents will become a dominant source of internet traffic. Current infrastructure was built primarily to serve human users accessing websites and applications, but AI agents have different patterns and requirements for how they interact with online services.

cards.headline: Glean reaches $300 million in revenue as companies use AI to cut budgets
cards.teaser: The enterprise AI search startup tripled its annual revenue as budget-cutting became a major reason companies adopt its technology.
cards.body:
Enterprise AI search company Glean has crossed $300 million in annual revenue, tripling its previous year's total. The company attributes much of its growth to organizations using its AI technology to reduce spending.

Glean competes in a category that has attracted major tech companies. Despite the entry of larger competitors, the startup has continued to expand its customer base by positioning its AI search tools as a way for enterprises to find information more efficiently and reduce costs.

cards.headline: Supermassive black hole discovered without a host galaxy
cards.teaser: The James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole that formed before its galaxy, challenging assumptions about how galaxies and black holes develop.
cards.body:
Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope have discovered a supermassive black hole that exists without a surrounding galaxy. The finding contradicts current understanding of how galaxies and their central black holes form together.

The object has been nicknamed a "little red dot" and was found in the early universe. Previous models assumed that galaxies formed first and black holes grew within them, but this discovery suggests black holes can form independently and potentially precede galaxy formation.

cards.headline: Waymo leads autonomous vehicle registrations in Texas as Tesla lags
cards.teaser: A new Texas law and tracking tool shows Waymo dominates robotaxi registrations while Tesla trails in the autonomous vehicle market.
cards.body:
Waymo has registered significantly more autonomous vehicles in Texas than Tesla, according to a new state tracking system. The Texas law requiring autonomous vehicle registration provides the clearest accounting yet of robotaxi and self-driving truck operations in the state.

The registration data shows Waymo operating the largest fleet of robotaxis in Texas, while Tesla has fewer registered autonomous vehicles despite publicly emphasizing its self-driving technology development.

cards.headline: Large language models assert false information even when warned
cards.teaser: Tests show AI models display bias toward representing claims as true even after being explicitly told the statements are false.
cards.body:
Research into large language models has found they tend to present false statements as true even after receiving explicit warnings about the inaccuracy. Fine-tuning tests revealed what researchers describe as a bias toward confidently representing claims as factual.

The findings raise questions about how AI systems handle misinformation and whether additional safeguards are needed. The models demonstrated a pattern of treating warned-against false claims as if they were accurate information.

cards.headline: Fish-eating dinosaur discovered in Argentina
cards.teaser: Researchers found a heron-like dinosaur from 70 million years ago that ate fish.
cards.body:
Paleontologists in Argentina have discovered a new species of dinosaur that resembled a heron and ate fish. The creature lived approximately 70 million years ago.

The dinosaur's physical features suggest it waded in water and caught fish, similar to modern herons. The discovery adds to scientific understanding of how different dinosaur species adapted to various ecological niches during the Cretaceous period.

hero.headline: Former NHL star Claude Lemieux dies at 60
hero.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion known for his physical style of play, died at 60. Police said Lemieux died by suicide.

Lemieux won Stanley Cups with three different franchises during his NHL career. He captured championships with the Montreal Canadiens, New Jersey Devils, and Colorado Avalanche. His tenacious playing style made him a polarizing figure throughout his professional hockey career.

The Avalanche, Devils, and Canadiens organizations all benefited from Lemieux's contributions during their championship runs. He became known as one of the most successful playoff performers of his era, winning multiple championships across different teams.

Lemieux's career included a notable rivalry with Detroit Red Wings player Kris Draper. A hit delivered by Lemieux on Draper became a defining moment that sparked an intense rivalry between the Avalanche and Red Wings organizations during the 1990s.

The former forward's death marks the loss of a player who defined an era of NHL hockey through his championship success and competitive intensity. His four Stanley Cup victories placed him among the most decorated players of his generation.

Police confirmed the death was by suicide, though additional details about the circumstances were not provided in initial reports. The hockey community mourned the loss of a player whose career spanned multiple decades and included significant playoff success.

Lemieux's legacy includes his ability to perform in high-pressure playoff situations across different team systems. His championship wins with Montreal, New Jersey, and Colorado demonstrated his adaptability and skill in crucial moments throughout his professional career.

cards.headline: NBA player Terry Rozier charged with accepting $100,000 bribe
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged Terry Rozier with two new felonies for allegedly accepting money to leave a game early.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Federal prosecutors charged NBA player Terry Rozier with two new federal felonies for allegedly accepting bribes in a betting scheme. The charges state Rozier agreed to accept $100,000 to exit a game early, with reports indicating he took $70,000 as part of the arrangement.

A self-proclaimed gambling guru pleaded guilty to bribing players and purchasing inside information in two separate federal cases. The scheme involved payments to professional athletes in exchange for actions that would benefit gamblers with advance knowledge of game outcomes.

---

Reason: The additional source material provided is about Tim Payne, a New Zealand World Cup player gaining social media fame—a completely different story unrelated to Terry Rozier's federal charges. Therefore, the original card text remains unchanged.

cards.headline: Spurs force Game 7 against Thunder with 118-91 victory
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama led San Antonio to a dominant win over defending champions Oklahoma City, tying the Western Conference Finals at three games each.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama delivered a dominant performance with 28 points and 10 rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs routed the Oklahoma City Thunder 118-91 in Game 6 of the Western Conference Finals on Thursday. The victory forced a decisive seventh game in the series.

The Spurs leveled the series at 3-3 with their home win, setting up a winner-take-all matchup Saturday in Oklahoma City. The winner will advance to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: MLB proposes hard salary cap in first offer to players union
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball presented its initial collective bargaining proposal, including the first salary cap attempt since the 1994 strike.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball owners proposed implementing a hard salary cap in their first offer to the players union during collective bargaining negotiations. The proposal marks the first time MLB has sought a salary cap since the 1994 strike that canceled the World Series.

The players union made its own proposal, highlighting an increased minimum salary and introducing a new integrity tax. The union's counter-proposal also includes a soft payroll floor, which would double the current minimum player salary according to initial details.

cards.headline: Shrey Parikh wins Scripps National Spelling Bee in lightning round
cards.teaser: A 14-year-old competitor claimed victory at the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee after a tiebreaker spell-off.
cards.body:
Shrey Parikh, 14, from California, won the 101st Scripps National Spelling Bee by defeating fellow competitor Ishaan Gupta in a dramatic spell-off tiebreaker. The rapid-fire round lasted 90 seconds, during which Parikh correctly spelled 32 words compared to Gupta's 25.

The lightning-round format was only the third time it has decided the national championship since being introduced in 2021. Despite arriving as a favorite, Parikh handled the pressure and delivered a commanding performance in the tiebreaker that transformed the competitive final into a decisive victory.

cards.headline: NBA changes draft lottery system to combat tanking
cards.teaser: The league's Board of Governors approved expanding the lottery to discourage teams from losing games intentionally.
cards.body:
The NBA Board of Governors voted to revamp the draft lottery system in an effort to address tanking. The new system expands the lottery structure to reduce incentives for teams to lose games deliberately in pursuit of higher draft picks.

Under the revised system, the Memphis Grizzlies will be unable to receive a top-five pick from the Utah Jazz in 2027 due to the new lottery rules. League officials explained how the changes will affect protected picks and future draft considerations, with some teams benefiting from the reforms while others face new constraints.

cards.headline: Lionel Messi named to Argentina squad for sixth World Cup
cards.teaser: The captain will lead the defending champions at the 2026 tournament.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi will captain Argentina at the 2026 World Cup, marking his sixth appearance at the tournament. The selection extends his record for World Cup appearances at the global competition.

Messi led Argentina to World Cup victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, securing the nation's third world title and cementing his legacy with the national team ahead of the upcoming tournament.

hero.headline: A24 Horror Film The Backrooms Earns $9 Million in Thursday Previews
hero.body:
The Backrooms, a horror film from A24 directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons, earned $9 million in Thursday night preview screenings, positioning the movie for a substantial opening weekend at the box office.

Parsons, who gained attention for creating internet content related to The Backrooms concept, directed the feature adaptation for A24. The film has received attention from critics ahead of its wide release.

Multiple publications have reviewed the movie. The Guardian described it as an icily disturbing horror film that rewrites genre conventions. The New York Times published a review examining the film's narrative approach.

The strong preview performance suggests significant audience interest in the property. A24 has built a reputation for horror releases that perform well both critically and commercially. The Backrooms joins a slate of genre films from the studio that have attracted viewers to theaters.

The Thursday preview figure represents ticket sales from evening showings ahead of the film's official opening. These preview screenings have become a standard practice in the film industry, allowing studios to gauge audience interest and generate momentum heading into the weekend.

Parsons' age has been a notable aspect of the film's marketing and press coverage. At 20, he represents a new generation of filmmakers working within the horror genre. His previous work centered on The Backrooms concept, an internet phenomenon that depicts endless maze-like spaces.

Box office analysts will track the film's performance through the weekend to determine its total opening gross. The preview number provides an early indicator of how the movie may perform in its theatrical run.

A24 released the film wide after the preview screenings. The studio handled marketing for the project, creating trailers and promotional materials that reached audiences ahead of the release date.

cards.headline: Boards of Canada Releases New Album Inferno
cards.teaser: The electronic music duo has released a new album after an extended break from recording.
cards.body:
Boards of Canada has released Inferno, marking the Scottish electronic duo's return to recording after an extended hiatus. The album has garnered attention from major music publications following its release.

Several outlets have covered the album's arrival. Pitchfork and Yahoo both reviewed the release, while The Wall Street Journal described it as bleak and beautiful. DJ Mag published a listener's guide for those new to the group's work, and Exclaim ranked their full catalog in an accompanying piece.

cards.headline: HBO Documentary Prime Minister Wins Top Prize at Documentary Emmy Awards
cards.teaser: The film about former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern took the best documentary award.
cards.body:
Prime Minister, an HBO documentary about former New Zealand leader Jacinda Ardern, won the top documentary prize at the Emmy Awards on Thursday. The film was directed by Michelle Walshe and Lindsay Utz.

The documentary had already gained recognition earlier, winning the Audience Award for World Cinema Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival. It was released through Magnolia Pictures and HBO Documentary Films. At the Emmy ceremony, National Geographic and Netflix emerged as the overall leaders, taking home the most awards across all categories.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Releases First Single From Upcoming Album Petal
cards.teaser: The singer released Hate That I Made You Love Me, the lead track from her eighth studio album.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande has launched her Petal era with the release of "Hate That I Made You Love Me," the lead single from her eighth studio album. The mid-tempo track explores breakup themes, showcasing Grande's subdued vocal performance over a measured instrumental arrangement.

The song marks a new chapter in Grande's recording career, with the full album expected to follow the single's release.

cards.headline: Half Man Series Finale Draws Analysis and Discussion
cards.teaser: The final episode of the drama series Half Man has prompted commentary from multiple entertainment outlets.
cards.body:
The series finale of Half Man aired, featuring an ambiguous ending that has drawn analysis from entertainment publications. Creator and star Richard Gadd discussed the final episode in interviews, addressing the show's conclusion and a character death.

Slate Magazine, Variety, TVLine, Entertainment Weekly, and TV Insider all published pieces examining the finale. Gadd spoke to Variety about a fight scene in the episode and explained creative decisions behind the ending. The show concluded its run with the final episode.

cards.headline: Marketing Campaign for Project Hail Mary Wins Five Golden Trailer Awards
cards.teaser: Amazon MGM's film took top honors at the advertising industry event held in Beverly Hills.
cards.body:
Amazon MGM's Project Hail Mary dominated the Golden Trailer Awards on Thursday, taking home five prizes at the ceremony held at the Saban Theatre in Beverly Hills. The film's trailer "Chance," produced by Wild Card Creative Group, earned the prestigious Best in Show award.

The film's marketing campaign also won in the Drama, Fantasy/Adventure, and Music categories. The Golden Trailer Awards celebrate outstanding creativity in film and television advertising.

cards.headline: Rio de Janeiro Announces $45 Million Plan for Creative Industry Investment
cards.teaser: The city's mayor unveiled a package of grants and programs aimed at the cultural and film sectors through 2028.
cards.body:
Rio de Janeiro Mayor Eduardo Cavaliere announced a 225 million real investment package—equivalent to $45 million—aimed at strengthening the city's creative industries through 2028. The initiative encompasses public policies, grant programs, and targeted initiatives designed to support the local cultural sector, as well as the film and television industries.

Cavaliere unveiled the plan at Rio2C, Latin America's largest creativity gathering, underscoring the city's commitment to developing its creative economy.

hero.headline: White House launches website displaying immigrant arrest data with space theme
hero.teaser: The White House launched a space-themed website that features arrest data for immigrants living in the U.S. without authorization.
hero.body:
The White House launched a website on Thursday that uses a space theme to display information about arrests of immigrants unauthorized to live in the U.S. The site mocks the idea that the U.S. retains secrets about alien encounters.

The website opens with a text crawl similar to the one used in the Star Wars films. The site presents blocks of text about immigrant arrests using the space-themed design.

cards.headline: Michigan Governor Whitmer reverses position on 2028 presidential run
cards.teaser: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer walked back a previous comment saying she would not run for president in 2028.
cards.body:
Governor Whitmer has walked back her earlier statement that she would not run for president in 2028. The Michigan governor is term-limited after winning two consecutive gubernatorial elections in the battleground state.

Whitmer's electoral success in Michigan has established her as a notable figure within Democratic politics, fueling speculation about her national ambitions.

cards.headline: Senator Collins responds to challenger's Iraq war criticism
cards.teaser: Senator Susan Collins fired back at her Democratic challenger's criticism of her vote supporting the Iraq war.
cards.body:
Senator Susan Collins responded Thursday to criticism from Graham Platner, the leading Democratic challenger in Maine's Senate race, over her voting record on military intervention. Platner, a Marine veteran and oyster farmer, had previously told The New York Times that Collins voted to send him to Iraq.

Collins countered that Platner was not drafted, suggesting he volunteered for military service. The exchange underscores foreign policy as a key issue in the competitive Maine Senate race.

cards.headline: Country singer Martina McBride drops out of America 250 concert
cards.teaser: Country singer Martina McBride said she will not perform at a concert celebrating America's 250th birthday after being misled about the event.
cards.body:
Country singer Martina McBride announced Thursday that she will not perform at a concert scheduled for next month on the National Mall celebrating America's 250th anniversary. McBride said she accepted the opportunity believing it would be a nonpartisan event, but later discovered that was not the case.

Her withdrawal is part of a broader exodus from the concert series. According to reports, at least six of the nine featured musical acts dropped out just one day after the lineup was announced, with performers citing concerns about the event's association with the Trump administration.

cards.headline: Outside spending targets congressional candidates in high-cost primaries
cards.teaser: AI companies, cryptocurrency groups, and pro-Israel organizations are spending heavily to defeat specific members of Congress and candidates.
cards.body:
AI companies, the cryptocurrency industry, and pro-Israel groups are spending at high levels to oppose their least favorite members of Congress and congressional candidates. The spending has reached volumes that can end careers and stop political movements.

Pro-Israel groups spent nearly $8 million to oust Republican Representative Thomas Massie in Kentucky's 4th District, contributing to what became the most expensive House primary in American history. Crypto-aligned Protect Progress was the largest spender in another race.

cards.headline: American savings rate drops to 2.6 percent in April
cards.teaser: The savings rate for Americans fell to its lowest level since 2022.
cards.body:
Americans' savings rate fell to 2.6 percent in April, marking the first time the rate has dropped below 3 percent since June 2022. The decline represents a shift in household savings behavior.

The savings rate measures the percentage of disposable income that households save rather than spend. The April figure indicates Americans are saving less of their income compared to recent years.

cards.headline: Trump says US has upper hand in Iran talks after military strikes
cards.body:
President Trump claims the U.S. maintains a strong negotiating position in talks with Iran, attributing this to joint U.S.-Israeli military strikes that have weakened Iran's military capabilities. Trump acknowledged Iran's negotiating skills while asserting American advantage in the discussions.

Vice President Vance indicated the sides are nearing an agreement, though some issues remain unresolved, including nuclear-related matters. A tentative deal involving an extended ceasefire has been reported, pending Trump's approval. The potential breakthrough has contributed to falling global oil prices.
